abstract: Obesity reflects chronic imbalance between energy storage and expenditure, yet how abundant circulating carrier proteins contribute remains poorly understood. Using constitutive and inducible albumin-deficient mice, we show that reduced circulating albumin promotes diet-induced adiposity and hepatic lipid accumulation while impairing energy expenditure, cold tolerance and stimulus-induced lipid mobilization. Recombinant mouse serum albumin (rMSA) restores thermogenic capacity and alleviates obesity, with anti-adiposity effects partly dependent on UCP1. Mechanistically, rMSA promotes brown-adipocyte thermogenic maturation through Cav1-associated Src-PI3K/AKT-mTORC1 signaling. Independently, the fatty-acid-to-albumin balance tunes beta3-adrenergic responsiveness: high fatty-acid loading shifts Cav1-associated complexes from beta3-AR toward CD36, whereas CD36 depletion restores beta3-AR association, PKA/HSL signaling and glycerol release. Glycation or oxidation impairs albumin fatty-acid binding and is associated with reduced metabolic efficacy. Thus, albumin abundance, fatty-acid loading and biochemical integrity jointly shape brown-adipose thermogenesis and obesity susceptibility.
